channel.title: HotsBuzz
channel.description: DIY projects, DIY ideas, crafts and more

item.title: DIY Christmas Wreath with Fresh or Faux Greenery
item.description: Bundle greenery onto a wire frame for a full, fragrant wreath that looks florist-made and costs a fraction of the price.

item.title: Pinecone Place Card Holders and Acorn Table Decor
item.description: Foraged pinecones become sturdy name card holders, and a bowl of acorns fills in the rest of the table. Natural, cheap and ready in an afternoon.

item.title: DIY Teacup Candles with Scented Soy Wax
item.description: Thrifted teacups and simple soy wax become a charming, practical gift. Here’s how to melt, scent and pour them safely.

item.title: DIY Fall Leaf Garland with Preserved Real Leaves
item.description: Real autumn leaves, preserved so they stay soft and colorful, strung on twine for your mantel, doorway or Thanksgiving table.

item.title: Cheesecloth Ghosts: Spooky Floating Halloween Decor
item.description: Stiffened cheesecloth dries into airy, free-standing ghosts that look eerie in a window or glowing over an LED light.

item.title: Thrifted Frame Gallery Wall With Painted Frames
item.description: Mismatched secondhand frames become a cohesive thrifted frame gallery wall with a coat of paint, paper templates and a little planning.

item.title: DIY St. Patrick’s Day Wreath with Burlap & Ribbon
item.description: Ruffled green burlap, plaid ribbon and a simple shamrock sign come together in a full, front-door-ready wreath you can reuse every March.

item.title: How to Make a Thanksgiving Gratitude Tree
item.description: A jar of bare branches, a stack of paper leaves and a pen by the door. By Thanksgiving Day, the tree is full of everything your family is thankful for.

item.title: Paper Bat Wall Decor: A Swarm of 3D Halloween Bats
item.description: Black cardstock bats with folded wings make a striking swirl across a wall, and they come down cleanly after Halloween.

item.title: Kindness Rocks: Easy Hand-Painted Rock Art
item.description: Smooth stones, bright paint and a short message are all it takes to make someone smile. Here’s how to paint rocks that survive the weather.

item.title: Valentine Mason Jar Gift: Sugar Scrub & Love Notes
item.description: Two easy ways to fill a mason jar for someone you love: a fragrant homemade sugar scrub or a jar stuffed with rolled-up love notes.

item.title: Paper Pumpkin Craft with Easy Paper Strips
item.description: Twelve strips of cardstock and two brads turn into a round, cheerful pumpkin you can make in any color and size.

item.title: Homemade Salt Dough Ornaments That Last for Years
item.description: A three-ingredient dough, a few cookie cutters and a slow bake give you sweet keepsake ornaments the whole family can make.

item.title: DIY Macrame Plant Hanger for Beginners
item.description: Learn three simple knots and make a macrame plant hanger that holds a 6-inch pot, using just cotton cord, a wooden ring and an afternoon.

item.title: Rainbow Pot of Gold Craft for Kids
item.description: Paper-strip rainbows, fluffy cotton clouds and a shiny pot of gold make this a cheerful St. Patrick’s Day project for little hands.

item.title: Paper Heart Wreath and Heart Garland DIY
item.description: Dozens of folded paper hearts layered into a full, fluttery wreath, plus a quick garland with the leftovers.

item.title: DIY Pressed Flower Bookmarks (No Resin Needed)
item.description: Turn a handful of garden blooms into bookmarks that last for years, sealed with simple laminating sheets instead of messy resin.

item.title: Rustic Wood Bead Garland With Tassels
item.description: A rustic wood bead garland with soft yarn tassels adds texture to shelves, trays and mantels, and it takes just an evening to string.

item.title: How to Make a Scandinavian Paper Star Decoration
item.description: Two squares of paper, a few straight cuts and a dab of glue become a crisp 3D star that looks beautiful in a winter window.

item.title: DIY Valentine Pop-Up Heart Card Tutorial
item.description: Open the card and a layered heart springs off the page. It looks clever, but it’s just two cuts, a few folds and some glue.
